subtopic: Share Class Fees and Investment Returns
source_evidence: This means that owning a different class of the same fund will result in different investment returns.
answer: Mutual fund share classes invest in the same portfolio, but they can charge different fees and expenses. Those costs affect returns: paying more fees leaves less money invested in the fund, and the impact of different fees can compound over time. When comparing classes, consider both any sales charges and ongoing expenses—not just the initial cost—because the class with the lowest upfront fees may not have the lowest costs over time.
